content: 1. Exercise caution and monitor when using cordyceps with prednisolone, as cordyceps may reduce the effects of prednisolone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Cordyceps has been observed to protect T and NK cells from the immunosuppressive effects of certain drugs. 2. Closely monitor the combination of protamine and cordyceps, as both agents can enhance anticoagulation effects. Therapy modification may be necessary. 3. Exercise caution and closely monitor when combining cordyceps with reishi, as both substances can increase anticoagulation effects. Therapy modification may be required. 4. Closely monitor the use of reteplase with cordyceps, as both agents can potentiate anticoagulation. Therapy adjustments may be needed. 5. Exercise caution and closely monitor when combining non-ASA salicylates with cordyceps, as both can enhance anticoagulation effects. 6. Closely monitor the combination of salsalate and cordyceps, as both agents can increase anticoagulation. Use caution. 7. Exercise caution and closely monitor when using cordyceps with Siberian ginseng, as both substances can enhance anticoagulation effects. 8. Cordyceps may reduce the toxicity of streptomycin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Closely monitor the combination of sulfasalazine and cordyceps, as both agents can increase anticoagulation. Use caution. 10. Exercise caution and closely monitor when combining sulindac with cordyceps, as both substances can enhance anticoagulation effects. 11. Closely monitor the use of tenecteplase with cordyceps, as both agents can potentiate anticoagulation. Therapy modification may be necessary. 12. Cordyceps may reduce the toxicity of tobramycin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 13. Exercise caution and closely monitor when using tolfenamic acid with cordyceps, as both agents can enhance anticoagulation effects. 14. Closely monitor the combination of tolmetin and cordyceps, as both substances can increase anticoagulation. Use caution. 15. Cordyceps may enhance the effects of tranylcypromine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, cordyceps falls under Pregnancy Category N/A and Lactation Category N/A. It is generally considered acceptable for use. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
